title: Implement ruby-version PEG and ruby-vercmp
description: Implement RubyGems-compatible parsing and comparison in src/init.janet. Add public ruby-version PEG and ruby-vercmp, preserving arbitrary-length numeric correctness and Gem::Version normalization/ordering semantics.
design: Build on numbers-compare where possible, but represent numeric segments as digit strings. Normalize whitespace and '-' as '.pre.' before segmentation; canonicalize trailing zero segments and leading zero segments before letters; compare numbers numerically, strings lexically, strings before numbers, and missing trailing segments according to Gem::Version#<=>.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation passes the Ruby compatibility matrix and maintains existing Debian, SemVer, and Maven behavior without regressions.
notes: Corrected missing-tail direction after direct oracle comparison: when the left version ends, a remaining string in the right means left is greater (release > prerelease); when the left has a remaining string, left is less. Numeric nonzero tails remain greater than a missing tail. Direct Janet probes and the full suite now pass.
close_reason: Applied missing-tail correction, direct probes match Gem::Version ordering for tested cases, and jpm -l test passes.

title: Design ruby-version PEG and segment representation
description: Design a Janet PEG named ruby-version that reflects Gem::Version's anchored VERSION_PATTERN and produces an explicit representation suitable for normalization and comparison, including the Gem hyphen-to-.pre. transformation.
design: Keep PEG responsibilities explicit and testable. The parser should consume the entire string, allow leading/trailing whitespace and an empty version as Gem::Version does, reject malformed separators/characters, and preserve digits and ASCII letter runs so numeric comparison can remain arbitrary precision.
acceptance_criteria: The representation and grammar are recorded in Beads and can distinguish numeric runs, ASCII letter runs, separators, and prerelease markers for every valid input class.
notes: Implementation detail clarified during PEG prototype: because Janet PEG matching is prefix-oriented unless explicitly anchored, ruby-version's :main must end with -1. A capture per alphanumeric base/suffix component is insufficient for segment output because Gem::Version scans each component into digit/letter runs; the public PEG should therefore use captures/replacements that emit tagged [:number digits] and [:string letters] nodes while enforcing complete consumption. Hyphens are best normalized in a transform before running the PEG, or represented by a separate suffix parser that emits .pre. string segments.
close_reason: Completed PEG design; anchored full-consumption behavior and segment emission details captured in notes.

title: Research Gem::Version source and define compatibility matrix
description: Read the RubyGems Gem::Version documentation and authoritative source, record the accepted grammar, normalization, canonical segments, prerelease handling, comparison rules, and malformed-input behavior needed for Janet compatibility.
design: Use the supplied Ruby docs plus RubyGems source and executable Ruby probes as the authority. Capture notable differences between current Ruby master docs and the installed RubyGems implementation where relevant, then choose and document the target behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A Beads note records the authoritative rules and representative expected comparisons, including whitespace, blank, hyphen, letter/digit, trailing-zero, malformed, and non-ASCII cases.
notes: Research complete. Gem::Version::VERSION_PATTERN is [0-9]+(?>\.[0-9a-zA-Z]+)*(-[0-9A-Za-z-]+(\.[0-9A-Za-z-]+)*)? with anchored surrounding whitespace and an optional whole version, so blank/whitespace normalizes to "0". initialize strips whitespace and replaces every '-' with '.pre.'. partition_segments scans digit runs as numeric segments and ASCII letter runs as string segments, dropping punctuation except that '.' controls grammar. canonical_segments removes trailing .0 segments and zero segments immediately before first letter in prereleases. <=> compares segment pairs: strings sort before numbers; numeric strings compare numerically; missing tail equals zero-only segments but is greater than remaining string segments. Docs state mixed alpha/digits split (a10 > a9) and prereleases sort below releases. Probes confirmed: 1 == 1.0 == 1.0.0; 1.0.0.a == 1.0.a; 1.0.a10 > 1.0.a9; 1.0 > 1.0.a1; 1.0.b1 > 1.0.a2; 1.0-a1 == 1.0.pre.a1; malformed 1..2, .1, 1., 1-, 1_2, 1+2, 1.é reject. Target ruby-version should return normalized segment strings/tags while ruby-vercmp mirrors ordering without machine integer limits.
close_reason: Completed source/documentation research and recorded the compatibility matrix in the issue notes.

title: Implement RubyGems Gem::Version compatibility and release 0.4.0

Keep Beads updated throughout and push Beads changes when complete.
design: Use a PEG that accepts the anchored RubyGems VERSION_PATTERN shape (including surrounding whitespace and blank input) and returns the normalized segment stream needed by Gem::Version ordering. Mirror Gem::Version#initialize hyphen-to-.pre. normalization, #canonical_segments, #partition_segments, and #<=> without relying on machine-sized integer conversion for numeric segments. Preserve the library's established comparator contract: negative, zero, or positive result.
acceptance_criteria: ruby-version and ruby-vercmp are public and documented; behavior is covered against Ruby Gem::Version for valid and malformed inputs; all Janet tests, docs generation, and package validation pass; project metadata is 0.4.0; changes are committed and tagged v0.4.0; all child beads are closed with notes.

Janet results matched for: 1.0 == 1.0.0; 1.0 > 1.0a1; 1.0a10 > 1.0a9; 1.0b1 > 1.0a2; 1.0.0.a == 1.0.a; 1.0-rc1 == 1.0.pre.rc1; and 1.0 < 1.0.0.1. title: Design maven-version PEG from ComparableVersion behavior
description: Define a PEG-compatible Maven version grammar and representation that preserves separators, numeric/text transitions, hyphen sublists, qualifiers, aliases, and combinations needed for comparison.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Design direction from wiki research: maven-version must preserve nested hyphen/list structure, ASCII numeric runs, text runs, text+digits combinations, and normalization-relevant zero/empty components. maven-vercmp will compare tagged nested nodes recursively rather than flattening Maven syntax.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Concrete PEG representation: maven-version returns a top-level [:list items] tree. Numeric runs are [:number digit-string] (retain stripped/original digits for arbitrary precision); text runs are [:string lowercased-text]; text immediately followed by digits is [:combination text digit-string]; hyphen-separated sections and text-after-dot sections are nested [:list items]. Dots continue the current list; hyphens create child lists except text-hyphen-digit, which is a combination. Comparison will normalize trailing null/zero nodes separately.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Constraint from maintainer: reuse the existing string-based numbers-compare helper for all Maven numeric node comparisons. It trims leading zeroes and compares by normalized length/content, so Maven need not duplicate arbitrary-precision numeric comparison.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Executable architecture: use maven-version's PEG as a lexer/parser for ASCII digit runs, non-digit runs, dots, and hyphens; a Janet builder then folds tokens into the tagged nested tree. This keeps context-sensitive X-1 combination handling and nested list creation explicit and testable, while the public binding remains a PEG-backed maven-version parser.
